title: Rapid production of much randomness indicates intrinsic generation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rapid production of much randomness indicates intrinsic generation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Whenever a large amount of randomness is produced in a short time, intrinsic randomness generation is overwhelmingly likely to be responsible, because it uses every component of a system to produce new randomness and has no length limit, whereas environmental amplification is slow and initial-condition randomness is short-lived.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The basic answer, I believe, is that whenever a large amount of randomness is produced in a short time, intrinsic randomness generation is overwhelmingly likely to be the mechanism responsible.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “The Intrinsic Generation of Randomness” (from p. 315), p. 321. Scope: natural and engineered systems that produce randomness

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-09: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.37

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claimed mechanism-frequency relationship is testable in principle with controlled repeated experiments. Public data are piecemeal and lack the interventions and population coverage required for the stated generality.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define production rate as entropy rate per active component and classify mechanisms using interventions that hold initial state fixed while shielding or varying environmental inputs. Across a representative sample, test whether high-rate systems overwhelmingly show repeatable deterministic internal generation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No representative dataset spans natural and engineered systems.

System boundaries determine what counts as intrinsic.

Existing observations rarely isolate all three mechanisms.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.22
operationalizability: 0.32
data existence: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.34
analysis feasibility: 0.32

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Engineered fast random-bit generators are the one place where rate and source are both documented well enough for a partial test, and some of those sources are amplified external or quantum noise. That comparison can challenge a universal reading of overwhelmingly likely without settling natural systems. The thresholds that define a large amount in a short time are not in the sentence, and natural cases lack the required paired observations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For systems that emit a declared large entropy in a declared short time, assign the source as intrinsic, environmental, or initial-condition, using device documentation and repeatability. A substantial class of fast emitters documented as amplified external noise would challenge overwhelmingly likely.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mechanism labels for natural systems are not deposited as a dataset.

Avalanche and quantum amplifiers produce randomness quickly from an external microscopic source.

Large amount and short time have no numerical thresholds in the text.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.32
data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.48
